name: Metallic Paint
rationale: Clean-room WebGL port written from the one-line effect description only (no upstream source read): a dependency-free fragment shader gives product cards and hero panels a flowing liquid-metal finish, with a static CSS gradient when WebGL is unavailable.

refract.description: How far the surface relief bends the reflected light.

chroma.description: Per-channel split of the reflection, for a thin-film colour fringe.

tint.description: Metal colour, as #rgb or #rrggbb; also tints the CSS fallback gradient.

speed.description: Flow speed; 0 holds a still frame.

scale.description: Size of the flow pattern; larger gives finer ripples.

a11y: The injected canvas is aria-hidden and pointer-events: none; the host's content, reading order and focus behaviour are unchanged.
The metal varies from dark to near-white, so text placed on it should sit on its own opaque or high-alpha scrim to keep 4.5:1 contrast (the demo does this).
Reduced motion stops the shader loop and the fallback sheen and shows one still frame of the metal.
Forced-colors mode hides the canvas and paints the host in Canvas/CanvasText with a visible border.
